collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — BELIEF, IDENTITY AND PERSONAL EXPRESSION (BLF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Religious, spiritual, atheist, agnostic, questioning and simply uninterested villagers living side by side; who people are, whom they love and how they present themselves. Privacy is respected, nobody has to explain or justify anything, and differences don't have to be the subject. Gods and spirits stay unconfirmed either way.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager invited to a feast does not eat pig, and pig is the main dish: say so quietly, or just eat the roots.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) has cooked a big feast and invited (subject). The main dish is a pig roasted with sweet roots. (subject) doesn't eat pig: it's part of what (subject.he/she) believes, and (subject.he/she) has never eaten it in (subject.his/her) life. (subject.He/she) looks at the steaming plate in front of (subject.him/her) and doesn't know what to say.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) leans over to (friend). "I'm sorry. I don't eat pig. It's my belief." (friend)'s eyes widen. "I didn't know! I'm so sorry." "It's alright," says (subject). "The sweet roots look wonderful." (friend) piles (friend.his/her) plate with roots and fruit and fish from the back. (subject) eats very well. Next time, (friend) asks first.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) quietly eats the sweet roots and leaves the pig. (friend) notices. Later (friend.he/she) asks, "Didn't you like it?" "I don't eat pig," says (subject). "It's part of what I believe. I didn't want to make a fuss." "You should have said," says (friend). "I'd have made fish." "Next time," says (subject). There is a next time. There is fish.
